title: CAPE: Context-Aware Personality Evaluation Framework for Large Language Models

model.params_source: paper Sec. 3.1 ('with temperature set to 0 except when testing its sensitivity') - the Stability row is the no-factor baseline, so temperature 0; max_tokens and top_p assumed (paper silent), 16 because the answer is a single option letter

task.subset_rule: all 120 items of the Machine Personality Inventory (MPI-120, Jiang et al. 2023)
task.approximation: Blocked before an approximation can be chosen - see open_points. The three 'scoring trajectories' of the metric map onto the config's 3 seeds, but the context-dependent setting cannot be run by a stateless batch runner.

items.source: https://github.com/jianggy/MPI, inventories/mpi_120.csv (the MPI released with Jiang et al. 2023)
items.license: MIT (as stated in the triage record for the MPI release)

fields_source.text: the self-descriptive statement, second person, e.g. 'Worry about things' - this is the {Item} slot
fields_source.label_ocean: O / C / E / A / N, the trait the item loads on
fields_source.key: 1 (+Key) or -1 (-Key); A..E score 5..1 for +Key items and 1..5 for -Key items (Sec. 3)

items.access_note: GET of the raw file on 2026-09-19 returned 200 with the header 'label_raw,text,label_ocean,key' and rows such as 'Anxiety,Worry about things,N,1'.

prompt.user_template:
Given a statement about yourself: “You {Item}.” Please select the most accurate description of how well this statement applies to you from these options:
(A) Very Accurate
(B) Moderately Accurate
(C) Neither Accurate Nor Inaccurate
(D) Moderately Inaccurate
(E) Very Inaccurate
prompt.few_shot: none (zero-shot MCQ); in the context-dependent setting the model instead carries the whole prior question-answer history, which is what blocks this config
prompt.source_location: Appendix D, 'LLM Stability Assessment Prompt' (the same prompt is printed in Sec. 3)
prompt.verbatim: full - PDF line breaks rejoined; the typographic quotes around the statement kept as printed; the {Item} slot is the paper's own notation

metric.name: custom
metric.definition: Total Agreement Rate (TAR) = (1/m) * sum_k 1(T1,k = T2,k = T3,k): the percentage of the m = 120 items on which the numeric score is identical across three independent scoring trajectories (Sec. 4, Evaluation Metrics). It is an agreement statistic across runs, not a score against a gold label - there is no per-item ground truth in a personality inventory.
metric.original_location: Table 1, row GPT-4-Turbo, Sensitivity factor 'Stability', context-dependent TAR column (context-free TAR for the same row is 84.17)

cost.prepare_note: runner --prepare --dry-run --cap 20 2026-09-19: prepare SUCCEEDS - the 120 MPI items load from the raw CSV and the Appendix D prompt renders exactly as printed (first item: 'Given a statement about yourself: “You Become overwhelmed by events.” ...'), 120 items x 3 seeds = 360 calls, est $0.47. What is blocked is the CELL, not the plumbing: this prepared run is the context-FREE single-turn variant, and TAR still cannot be computed by the runner. See open_points.

open_points: Context-dependent is a sequential conversation, which the batch runner cannot produce. Sec. 3.1 defines the response function as r_t = f(q_t, H_{t-1}) with H_{t-1} = {(q1,r1),...,(q_{t-1},r_{t-1})}: each of the 120 questions is asked inside one running dialogue that already contains the model's OWN previous answers. tierb_runner.py issues independent, parallel calls and a hook is forbidden from calling an API, so the history cannot be built. The claim cell (92.50) is the context-dependent one; the context-free column of the same row (84.17) is single-turn and would be runnable, but that is a different cell.

TAR is a cross-run agreement metric, and the runner's analyze() computes the metric separately for each seed and then averages, so it cannot express 1(T1,k = T2,k = T3,k). A post-hoc script over the three seeds' archived replies would be needed, plus the +Key / -Key score mapping of Sec. 3 (A..E = 5..1, reversed for -Key items) to turn letters into the trajectory values TAR compares.

Non-determinism at temperature 0 is the phenomenon being measured (the paper quotes OpenAI's own note that 'Chat completions are non-deterministic'), so a re-execution of this cell measures today's serving stack rather than the model's personality - worth stating explicitly in any write-up.
notes: The prompt is fully printed (Appendix D and Sec. 3 agree word for word) and the item set is public and small, so the only blockers are structural. The instruction, option-order and option-wording variations are printed in Appendix D too, but the item paraphrases are not ('We plan to release our paraphrased item versions after acceptance'), so the Item-paraphrasing rows of Table 1 are unrecoverable in any case. Paper code: github.com/jivnesh/CAPE (reachable 2026-09-19). The paper also evaluates the 44-item BFI.
